definition: A real-time object detection model that predicts bounding boxes and classes in a single pass over the image.
details: Unlike sliding-window detectors, YOLO reframes detection as a single regression problem: one network looks at the whole image and directly outputs boxes and class probabilities. This unified design made detection extremely fast while remaining accurate, enabling real-time video applications.

explainer.lead: YOLO is a real-time object detection model that predicts bounding boxes and classes in a single pass over the image. Its speed made detection practical for live video.

tiers.eli5: Instead of scanning a picture window by window, it glances at the whole thing once and points out what it sees.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it when detection latency matters, such as live video pipelines. A pitfall is small or clustered objects, which single-pass detectors can miss compared with slower multi-stage approaches.
tiers.paperLevel: Detection is framed as a single regression: one network maps the whole image to boxes and class probabilities in one forward pass; accuracy on small objects and tight localization is its known limit.

explainer.example: A security camera feeds frames to YOLO, which outputs boxes labelled person or car within milliseconds per frame.

citation.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
